questions.prompt: Which 4+1 view addresses concurrency, synchronization and performance at runtime?
questions.explain: **Process view** = runtime behavior (Sequence/Communication diagrams; integrators, performance engineers). Logical = functionality; Development = code organization; Physical = deployment to hardware.

questions.prompt: Mapping software onto hardware nodes/networks for scalability and availability is the job of the:
questions.explain: **Physical view** — Deployment/Infrastructure diagrams; stakeholders: system engineers, operators/DevOps.

questions.prompt: A presentation tier calls a business-logic tier which calls a data tier; each layer may only use the layer directly below. Which style?
questions.explain: **Layered**: hierarchical separation with strict usage rules — changes isolated per layer; classic 3-tier enterprise shape.

questions.prompt: Components publish events; subscribers react without the publisher knowing them. Which style, and its key benefit?
options: Event-driven — extreme decoupling of producers from consumers
questions.explain: **Event-driven** (publish/subscribe): producers don't know consumers → add/remove subscribers without touching publishers. (Observer is the same idea at object scale.)

questions.prompt: The DEFINING criterion that makes a system 'microservices' rather than a modular monolith is:
options: Services are INDEPENDENTLY DEPLOYABLE units behind stable interfaces
It has more than five classes
It uses a single shared database
questions.explain: **Independent deployability** (with independent scaling + fault isolation) is the defining property; one shared database would couple them again. Each service owns its data store and communicates via APIs/events.

questions.prompt: Adding encryption everywhere improves security but slows responses. This illustrates:
options: Quality attributes TRADE OFF against each other — the architect balances stakeholder concerns
Security is always the top priority
questions.explain: Architectural decisions trade quality attributes (security vs performance vs usability…). Managing these competing **influences/stakeholder concerns** is one of the architect's documented duties.

questions.prompt: In the blackboard style, the shared central data structure that all knowledge sources read and write is called the ______. (one word)
questions.explain: The style is NAMED after its central shared dataset — the **blackboard** — written/read opportunistically by independent knowledge sources under a controller.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of style → weakness is correct?
options: Client-server → the server is a bottleneck / single point of failure
Pipes and filters → cannot chain transformations
questions.explain: Client-server centralizes service provision: capacity and availability hinge on the server. The other pairings invert each style's actual STRENGTH.
